result.title: WCC: A Learning-Based Framework for Deciding When to Apply Cooperative Coevolution in Large-Scale Optimization
result.summary: Cooperative Coevolution (CC) and Non-Decomposition Algorithms (NDAs) are two primary approaches for large-scale global optimization (LSGO). Although both have achieved success, they exhibit markedly different performance across problem types and each faces approach-specific limitations, leaving the question of "when to use CC" unresolved. We address this gap with WCC, a novel learning-based framework that dynamically decides when to deploy CC in LSGO. WCC employs a streamlined design for efficient adaptive learning. We formulate the decision as a Markov decision process, designing a targeted feature set, a robust reward, and a tailored network architecture to provide the agent with rich information about the problem state and optimization progress. Our auto-regressive policy enables WCC to perform fine-grained, dynamic switching between CC and NDAs while conditionally allocating the computational budget without expert specifications. WCC shows strong competitiveness and superior generalization across problems, optimization horizons, and baseline optimizers. It realizes a "train-once and reuse" paradigm under a low budget, significantly curbing LSGO cost. Additionally, in-depth analyses yield insights not captured by existing theory, offering practical guidance on when and how to effectively deploy CC.

AI.brief_summary: 该文针对大规模全局优化中协同进化（CC）与非分解算法性能互补但「何时使用 CC」缺乏依据的问题，提出 WCC：把该决策建模为马尔可夫决策过程，设计问题状态特征、奖励与自回归策略，动态切换两类算法并无专家设定地分配计算预算。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「学习何时调用特定模块并分配预算」的元决策范式可能为 LVR 中 THINK／LOOK／STOP 的触发与计算分配提供可核查线索，但领域距离较远，需评估其特征与奖励设计能否迁移到视觉推理状态判断。
